answer: A network can require each agent to present a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after proof of personhood, then cap votes and rewards at one per credential. Fake accounts no longer multiply influence: an attacker must recruit real people or defeat verification, paying for each identity and risking detection and revocation. The credential is a marble token in an oasis of pseudonyms; scaling the attack becomes a gale of cost, not a cheap script.
